Bedding we’d shopped for together, posters and toiletries and a desk lamp. 
  I drove that eight hours north to upstate NY alone with him,  sneaking glances over at his face -which was occasionally napping, but often laughing -with such a sense of poignancy in my heart that at times, I thought it might stop beating. 
   This song, for me, is that last ride with my little boy where the chains were falling away.

"Orbiter" got to me in a way I can't even explain. This song doesn't just reach your ears; it reaches your soul. Noah Kahan has an incredible gift for turning feelings we can't even put into words into a song. 
 
The way he talks about being stuck—to people, emotions, and cycles, as if we’re constantly orbiting something we should have left behind—is painfully beautiful. It’s a song that embraces, hurts, and comforts all at once. 
 
Seriously... thank you for existing, Noah. This has become one of those songs I’ll carry with me for a long time.
